Answer: D
Reason: Comparing the initial chest radiograph (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung zone, with the follow-up radiograph (Figure 4) reveals significant progression characterized by new, bilateral patchy airspace opacities. This pattern of migratory or expanding multifocal consolidations is a hallmark radiographic feature of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP).
